0.1.n: Part of でございます, a very polite alternative to です.

0.2.n: The connecting form of ござる, used with で and ます for a very polite introduction.

0.3.n: Adds politeness to ござい; the full expression でございます formally identifies the speaker.

1.0.n: Refers to this video or installment rather than necessarily today.

1.1.n: Marks 今回 as the topic, setting the scope of this introduction.

1.2.n: Tells when the speaker stayed at the inns.

1.3.n: Past form of 宿泊する, placed before 温泉旅館 to describe inns the speaker stayed at.

1.4.n: Modifies 旅館 to specify inns with hot-spring bathing facilities.

1.5.n: Combines with 温泉 to name the type of accommodation being discussed.

1.6.n: Links 温泉旅館 to 中, identifying the group from which the inns are selected.

1.7.n: 中 refers to the group of inns, not their physical interiors.

1.8.n: Marks the pool from which the speaker selects five inns.

1.10.n: Emphasizes that these inns stood out compared with the others.

1.11.n: Past form of 良い; it describes the speaker’s experience of the inns.

1.12.n: A general word for lodging, referring here to the hot-spring inns.

1.13.n: 軒 counts houses and establishments, including inns.

1.14.n: Marks the five inns as what the speaker carefully selects and introduces.

1.15.n: て-form of 厳選する, linking the careful selection to the following introduction.

1.16.n: ご紹介する is humble; してまいります politely signals proceeding with the introductions.

2.0.n: Names the assessment process whose method is explained next.

2.1.n: Marks 評価 as the topic of the explanation.

2.3.n: Names the accommodation itself as one scoring category.

2.5.n: Refers to the meals served, rather than the act of cooking.

2.7.n: Names the hot-spring bathing facilities as a scoring category.

2.9.n: Focuses on how staff receive and interact with guests.

2.11.n: Listed separately from 接客, this likely covers guest services beyond direct staff interaction.

2.13.n: Names the cost of staying as a scoring category.

2.15.n: Refers to sightseeing opportunities associated with each inn.

2.17.n: An English loanword used here for the inn’s setting or position.

2.18.n: Connects the entire preceding list to 8項目, identifying which eight categories are scored.

2.19.n: Gives the number of scoring categories.

2.20.n: Refers to the separate aspects assessed in the evaluation.

2.21.n: Marks the eight categories as what receives scores.

2.22.n: The linking form of 採点する connects scoring the categories with ranking the inns.

2.24.n: Combines with 得点 to refer to the combined result across categories.

2.25.n: Together with 総合, it names the total used to determine rankings.

2.26.n: Marks the overall score as the basis for ranking.

2.27.n: Combines ランク with 付け, assigning positions, and takes する to form a verb.

2.28.n: A humble, polite version of しています, presenting ranking as the speaker’s established practice.

0.tip: でございます is a very polite way to say です in a formal self-introduction.

1.lit: This time, from hot-spring inns stayed at this year, [I] carefully select and introduce five especially good inns.
1.tip: 宿泊した directly describes 温泉旅館: Japanese places descriptions like stayed at this year before the noun.

2.lit: Evaluation scores eight categories—inn, food, hot springs, hospitality, services, price, sightseeing, location—and ranks by overall score.
2.tip: The の after ロケーション links the whole eight-part list to 項目, not just the final item.
